meal.title: Limited Direct Execution Explained
meal.objective: Explain how the OS intervenes only when necessary under limited direct execution

voice.script: What if your computer only stepped in when it really had to? When does the OS actually take control of the CPU? Limited direct execution means the CPU runs user code until the OS must step in. Here is a tiny program that simulates a process running until a timer fires. The program loops through a list of process names, prints the current one, and after two iterations triggers a timer event. When the timer expires the OS switches to the next process. The flow diagram shows user code, then a timer interrupt, then the OS scheduler, then the next process. Remember: limited direct execution lets user code run freely until the OS needs to intervene. Add another timer event and see how the scheduler picks the next process.

visual.code:
processes = ['P1', 'P2', 'P3']
counter = 0
for name in processes:
    print(f'Running', name)
    counter += 1
    if counter == 2:
        print('Timer interrupt: OS takes over')
        counter = 0
        print('Scheduler selects next process')
